title: Denoising and Baseline Correction Methods for Raman Spectroscopy Based on Convolutional Autoencoder: A Unified Solution

citations.claim: Han et al. proposed a unified preprocessing pipeline for Raman spectroscopy consisting of a convolutional denoising autoencoder (CDAE) for noise reduction followed by a convolutional autoencoder with a comparison function (CAE+) for baseline correction.

Han et al. modeled Raman spectra as the sum of three components: Raman peaks generated by superposition of Lorentzian functions, a fluorescence background baseline, and random noise, expressed as y = y_r + b + n.

Han et al. incorporated a comparison function (element-wise minimum between input and decoder output) into the CAE+ baseline correction model, exploiting the prior knowledge that baseline values are typically lower than signal values at each point.

Han et al. demonstrated that their CAE+ model achieved significantly lower RMSE for baseline correction compared to airPLS and iterative polynomial fitting, with mean RMSE of 7.6 versus 61.6 and 71.6, respectively, on simulated spectra.

Han et al. showed that classical preprocessing algorithms such as Savitzky-Golay filtering and polynomial baseline correction reduce Raman peak intensities and alter peak shapes, while their CDAE-CAE+ approach better preserves peak characteristics.

Han et al. noted that the effectiveness of classical spectral denoising and baseline correction algorithms depends heavily on manual parameter selection, and the choice of parameters largely relies on operator experience.

Han et al. trained their models on synthetic spectra with Lorentzian peaks, Gaussian/sigmoid/polynomial baselines, and varying noise levels, using MSE as the loss function with early stopping to prevent overfitting.

Han et al. achieved peak preservation rates between 0.85 and 0.96 with their CDAE model, consistently outperforming Savitzky-Golay filtering and wavelet threshold denoising in maintaining Raman peak intensity.

do_not_claim: This paper does not use algorithm unrolling or deep unfolding
This paper does not address chromatogram baseline correction, only Raman spectroscopy
This paper does not demonstrate cross-device or cross-sample generalization
This paper does not use self-supervised or unsupervised learning for the preprocessing task despite using autoencoders; the training is supervised with synthetic data
